decisionMemo.businessProblem: A $1.5B commercial staffing firm has seen EBITDA margin fall from 8.0% to 6.0% (200 bps) in a single year even as reported revenue still grew +5%. Growth has decelerated sharply (from +12% to +5%), and the leading indicators of the staffing cycle are turning negative: permanent / direct-hire placement revenue (the canary for hiring demand) is down -8% YoY, client orders are down -6% YoY, and temp hours per week are trending -2% sequentially. At the same time, the firm has continued to add fixed capacity — internal recruiter/branch headcount grew +4% — and SG&A (~13.5% of revenue) remains largely fixed and was sized during the prior high-growth expansion. Gross spread also compressed 150 bps (21.0% to 19.5%) because worker wage inflation (+6%) outran the bill-rate increases the firm could push through to budget- and competition-constrained clients (+3.5%), leaving ~250 bps of unrecovered wage inflation on the temp book. The core challenge: is the 200 bps EBITDA decline primarily a controllable pricing/spread problem, a structural unit-economics breakdown, or a softening demand cycle that the cost base has been sized ahead of rather than adjusted to? The CEO must decide within ~90 days whether to freeze internal hiring and right-size branches ahead of a possible downturn, or hold capacity for a rebound — and a wrong call in either direction is materially costly.

Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
